2.The writ petitioner is running a petty shop in the petition- mentioned premises.

On 12.10.2025,
the police attached to Kallikudi police station inspected the petitioner's shop premises.
According to the jurisdictional police, the petitioner was keeping banned Gutkha products.

The writ petitioner was taken to the police station and Crime No.195 of 2025 was registered on the file of Kallikudi police station for the offences under Sections 296(b), 132, 123 BNS and 24(1) of the Cigarettes and other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce,

The petitioner's shop was also sealed and his food license was temporarily cancelled.
Challenging the same, this writ petition came to be filed.
3.The learned counsel appearing for the writ petitioner reiterated all the contentions set out in the affidavit filed in support of the writ petition and called upon me to grant relief as prayed for.

4.Per contra, the learned Government Advocate submitted that the the writ petitioner was a third time offender and therefore, the proceedings issued in R.No.8941/2019/S1/FSSA dated 02.07.2025 issued by the Commissioner of Food Safety, Chennai-6 would come into play.

S.Subramanian and Others), the Division Bench was concerned with a similar order dated 04.01.2024 issued by the Commissioner of Tamil Nadu Food Safety which provided for levy of compounding penalty for selling banned food items.

sentences.text: However, in the case on hand, I am concerned with the subsequent proceedings dated 02.07.2025 issued by the Commissioner of Food Safety which has already been extracted above.

7.The impugned action has three components:-
a) Suspension of the petitioner's food business license.
b) Sealing of his shop premises and c) Levy of compounding penalty.
8.As regards the first component, the petitioner will have to necessarily file an appeal or avail any other statutory remedy.
The scope of this writ petition is confined to testing the legality of sealing the premises and levying compounding penalty.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

8.What calls for consideration is whether the Commissioner of Food Safety could have authorised the Food Safety Officer to levy compounding penalty and seal the premises for a given period on the ground that the licensee has been implicated in a criminal case pertaining to food safety.
9.Let me take up the issue pertaining to levy of compounding penalty first.

It has already been held by the Division Bench in The Commissioner of Tamil Nadu Food Safety and Drug Administration Department and Others Vs. S.Subramanian (2025 2 Writ LR 454) that compounding is a consensual affair and that any person against whom a criminal case is registered is entitled to defend himself against the accusation and establish his innocence.

entities.text: Commissioner of Tamil Nadu Food Safety and Drug Administration Department and Others Vs. S.Subramanian (2025 2 Writ LR 454)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Paragraph No.9 of the said decision reads as follows:-
...When one is accused of having acted illegally, it is open to the accused to defend himself in the manner known to law.
One can either plead guilty or contest the charges.
Right to defend oneself against an accusation is a fundamental right.
The person accused cannot be compelled to admit that he or she committed the offence.

If the offender pays the compounding https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on:
21/01/2026 08:17:06 pm ) penalty, he can avoid prosecution.
If he does not, he has to face adjudication under Section 68 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 or face trial in the criminal court.
The choice is left to the individual.
Section 69 of the Act empowers the authority to compound offences.

It reads as follows :
69. Power to compound offences.-The Commissioner of Food Safety may, by order,

empower the Designated Officer, to accept from petty manufacturers who himself M.Thanga Muniyandi vs The Commissioner on 19 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101409126/
3 manufacture and sell any article of food, retailers, hawkers, itinerant vendors,
temporary stall holders against whom a reasonable belief exists that he has committed an offence or contravention against this Act, payment of a sum of money by way of composition of the offence which such person is suspected to have committed.

entities.text: M.Thanga Muniyandi vs The Commissioner on 19 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (2) On the payment of such sum of money to such officer, the suspected person, if in custody, shall be discharged and no further proceedings in respect of the offence shall be taken against such person.

(3) The sum of money accepted or agreed to be accepted as composition under sub section (1), shall not be more than one lakh rupees and due regard shall be made to the guidelines specified in section 49: Provided that no offence, for which punishment of imprisonment has been https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 21/01/2026 08:17:06 pm ) prescribed under this Act, shall be compounded.
....The authority cannot insist that unless the compounding penalty is paid, the shop will be sealed or not de-sealed.
That would amount to rank coercion.
... If the offender comes forward to compound the offence by paying the penalty, the official may accept the payment and close the prosecution.
It cannot be imposed on the accused.

Therefore, the authority was not justified in straightaway levying compounding penalty of Rs.1 Lakh on the petitioner merely on the ground that he has been implicated as an accused for the third time in an offence pertaining to food safety.
This point is answered accordingly.
10.The next issue pertains to the validity of the exercise of power of sealing.
The power to seal is not traceable to any provision in the The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
It is only found in Regulation 2.1.3.4 (i) of the Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011 which confers power to seal on the Food Safety Officer.

This Rule was interpreted by the Division Bench in in S.Subramanian case in the following terms :-
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

( Uploaded on: 21/01/2026 08:17:06 pm ) 4....The Rule itself reads that the premises may be sealed for investigation after the Food Safety Officer is of the opinion that in the given situation, it is not possible to comply with the provision of Section 38(1)(c) or the proviso to Section 38(1) for reasons like non-availability of the food business operator.
Section 38(1)(c) of the Act envisages keeping the seized food article in the custody of the food business operator.
The proviso to Section 38(1) empowers the Food Safety Officer in such cases to call upon the food business operator to execute a bond with sureties.
If the food business operator is not available, the Food Safety Officer will have no option but to seal the premises.
The sealing of premises is for the purpose of investigation.
5. It is well settled that the power to seal is a drastic power.
The Act and the Rules framed thereunder are both regulatory as well as penal in character.
Therefore, the Rule cannot be expansively or liberally construed.
On the other hand, it has to be strictly interpreted.
The application of the Rule will have to be within the four corners of the statute.

4 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 21/01/2026 08:17:06 pm )
7..Unless the twin conditions laid down in the Rule (A. The authority must be of the opinion that it is not possible to comply with the provision of Section 38(1)(c) or the proviso to Section 38(1) B.
Sealing is necessary for the purpose of investigation) are satisfied, any act of sealing will be without jurisdiction.

sentences.text: The expression "for" found in the Rule cannot be ignored.
P.Ramanatha Aiyar's Advanced Law Lexicon states that the word "for" is sometimes used as importing a condition precedent, or as a word of limitation.
It can also mean "in the interest" or "to the benefit of".
In the present context, it can only mean that sealing must facilitate investigation.
The authority is obliged to show that if sealing is not done, investigation will be hampered.
The investigation referred to is not investigation by police.
Since the Act contemplates further steps by the Food Safety Officer, the expression "investigation" would refer only to those steps to be taken by the Food Safety Officer and nothing else.
Further, the sealing of the premises cannot be for eternity.
The investigation has to be concluded within a reasonable time and once investigation is over, the premises must be de
-sealed.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
Thus, the power to seal can be invoked and exercised only for the purpose of investigation and not for any further purpose.
It is not the case of the third respondent that for the sake of investigation, the petitioner's premises have been sealed.

On the other hand, the Food Safety Officer entered the scene only after the criminal case was registered by the jurisdictional police and therefore, the question of the third respondent undertaking any investigation does not arise at all.

11.The stand of the learned Government Advocate is that the proceedings bearing R.No.8941/2019/S1/FSSA dated 02.07.2025 empowers the Food Safety Officer to seal the premises following the implication of the licensee in a criminal case.
It is seen that in the said proceedings, the Commissioner of Food Safety has traced his power to Section 30(3) read with Section 38(10) of the Act to issue the aforesaid proceedings.

Section 30(3) reads as follows:
30. Commissioner of Food Safety of the State- (1) ...
(2) ...
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

entities.text: Commissioner of Food Safety of the State-
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: (3) The Commissioner of Food Safety may, by Order, delegate, subject to such conditions and restrictions as may be specified in the Order, such of his powers and functions under this Act (except the power to appoint Designated Officer, Food Safety Officer and Food Analyst) as he may deem necessary or expedient to any officer subordinate to him.
It only enables the Commissioner of Food Safety to delegate any power that he/she is entitled to exercise.
Nowhere in the statute, the power of sealing has been conferred on the Commissioner of Food Safety.
Therefore, the question of delegating a non-existent power does not arise at all.
I have to see whether in Section 38(10) of the Act, such power has been conferred on the Food Safety Officer and the Commissioner of Food Safety.

Section 38(10) of the Act reads as follows:-
M.Thanga Muniyandi vs The Commissioner on 19 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101409126/
5 38. Powers of Food Safety Officer- ...
10) The Commissioner of Food Safety may from time to time issue guidelines with regard to exercise of powers of the Food Safety Officer, which shall be binding:
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 21/01/2026 08:17:06 pm )

entities.text: M.Thanga Muniyandi vs The Commissioner on 19 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Provided that the powers of such Food Safety Officer may also be revoked for a specified period by the Commissioner of Food Safety.
12.Section 38 confers certain powers on the Food Safety Officers.
In order to ensure that the power conferred is not arbitrarily exercised, the Commissioner of Food Safety has been empowered to prescribe and issue guidelines from time to time.
Such guidelines would be binding on the Food Safety Officer.

The scope of Section 38(10)
of the Act is confined to only prescribing a broad frame-work within which the Food Safety Officer is expected to exercise his statutory powers.
In other words, norms governing the power to exercise has to be laid down under this provision.
Section 38(10) of the Act does not and cannot authorise the Commissioner of Food Safety to confer some power on the Food Safety Officer which the statute has not conferred on him.
The power of sealing for any other purpose other than investigation has not been conferred on either the Commissioner of Food Safety or the Food Safety Officer.
Therefore, by the aforesaid proceedings dated 02.07.2025, such a power could not have been conferred.

One should not rush in where https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on:
21/01/2026 08:17:06 pm ) angels fear to tread.
The Commissioner of Food Safety is a statutory authority.
He has no inherent power.
He cannot venture into domains untrodden by the statute.
Philosopher Wittgenstein famously said whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must pass over in silence.
The executive authority may not endeavour to fill up the purported lacuna in the statute.
13.This issue can be looked at from another angle also.
It is the fundamental principle of law that no one can be subject to criminal sanction or penalty except under a clear authority of law.
In a civilized society governed by rule of law, the punishment not prescribed under the statutory rules cannot be imposed (Vijay Singh vs. State of U.P. and Ors, (2012) 5 SCC 242) .

entities.text: Vijay Singh vs. State of U.P. and Ors, (2012) 5 SCC 242
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The criminal sanction and penalties are to be laid down by the legislature in the parent law and the entity to whom the power to make rules is delegated cannot usurp that power.
It is not for the executive authority to define offences or contraventions and prescribe punishments or penalties in respect of such offences and contraventions.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
14.Section 38(10) of the Act merely empowers the Commissioner of Food Safety to prescribe the guidelines in the exercise of power by the Food Safety Officer.
He cannot travel beyond and confer additional power on the Food Safety Officer.
As already mentioned, the power to seal can be exercised only in certain prescribed circumstances under Regulation 2:1:3:4.

The Commissioner of Food Safety had authorised the Food Safety Officer to effect sealing merely because the licensee has M.Thanga Muniyandi vs The Commissioner on 19 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101409126/
6 been implicated in an offence.

entities.text: M.Thanga Muniyandi vs The Commissioner on 19 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This is not contemplated under the statutory scheme.
15.I am conscious that the petitioner has not formally impugned the validity of the proceedings dated 02.07.2025.
When the authorities rely on the proceedings dated 02.07.2025 in support of their action, I have to necessarily examine if they are valid.
Once I find the said proceedings to be patently without jurisdiction, I cannot shut my eyes.
I therefore have to necessarily rule on the legality of the aforesaid proceedings.
The impugned proceedings levying compounding penalty and sealing the petitioner's premises stand quashed.
The petitioner is given liberty to file an appeal challenging the suspension of his food business license.

If such an appeal is filed https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 21/01/2026 08:17:06 pm ) within a period of two weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order, it shall be entertained without limitation and disposed of on merits within eight weeks thereafter.
16.This writ petition is partly allowed.
No costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
